title: Oh Dear, What Can the Matter Be?
origin: English folk song, printed in Edinburgh and London c.1792 (Scots Musical Museum and broadsides); chorus only
publicDomainBasis: Traditional, no known author; published c.1792

title: Alouette
origin: French-Canadian folk song, first printed in A Pocket Song Book for the Use of Students and Graduates of McGill College (1879); refrain only, with in-house English words by Little Duet (the French words are about plucking a lark)
publicDomainBasis: Traditional tune, printed 1879; English words written in-house

title: Ode to Joy
origin: Ludwig van Beethoven, Symphony No. 9, finale theme (1824); simple English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Published 1824; Beethoven died 1827; English words written in-house

title: Oh! Susanna
origin: Stephen Foster (1848); first verse and chorus only
publicDomainBasis: Published 1848; Foster died 1864

title: On the Bridge of Avignon
origin: French folk song 'Sur le pont d'Avignon' (15th-century roots), popularised by Adolphe Adam's opera Le Sourd (1853); English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Traditional; arranged 1853 (Adam died 1856); English words written in-house

title: Over the River and Through the Wood
origin: Words by Lydia Maria Child, 'The New-England Boy's Song about Thanksgiving Day' (1844); traditional American tune, composer unknown
publicDomainBasis: Words published 1844, Child died 1880; tune traditional, in print before 1931

title: Shoo Fly, Don't Bother Me
origin: American song credited to T. Brigham Bishop (words) and Frank Campbell / Billy Reeves (1869); chorus only, with the original 1869 last line
publicDomainBasis: Published 1869; credited writers died before 1931

title: Up on the Housetop
origin: Words and music by Benjamin Hanby (1864)
publicDomainBasis: Published 1864; Hanby died 1867

title: All Through the Night
origin: Welsh melody 'Ar Hyd y Nos', first printed in Edward Jones, Musical and Poetical Relicks of the Welsh Bards (1784); English words by Harold Boulton (1884), first verse
publicDomainBasis: Melody published 1784; Boulton's words published 1884, Boulton died 1935 (words pre-1931 publication)

title: O Christmas Tree
origin: German carol 'O Tannenbaum', words Ernst Anschutz (1824) to a traditional folk tune; English words traditional and Little Duet (middle lines)
publicDomainBasis: Published 1824; Anschutz d.1861; tune traditional; middle lines written in-house

title: Surprise! (Haydn)
origin: Joseph Haydn, Symphony No. 94 'Surprise', Andante theme (1791); simple English words by Little Duet
publicDomainBasis: Published 1791; Haydn died 1809; English words written in-house

title: The Bear Went Over the Mountain
origin: Children's song sung to the tune of 'For He's a Jolly Good Fellow' (French 'Malbrough s'en va-t-en guerre', c.1780)
publicDomainBasis: Tune traditional, 18th century; words traditional, 19th century

title: The Twelve Days of Christmas (First Day)
origin: English cumulative carol, printed in Mirth without Mischief (c.1780); familiar tune arranged by Frederic Austin (1909); first day only
publicDomainBasis: Words c.1780; Austin arrangement 1909 (Austin d.1952)

title: Three Blind Mice
origin: Round printed by Thomas Ravenscroft in Deuteromelia (1609)
publicDomainBasis: Published 1609

title: She'll Be Coming Round the Mountain
origin: American folk song adapted from the spiritual 'When the Chariot Comes'; printed in Carl Sandburg's The American Songbag (1927)
publicDomainBasis: Traditional; printed 1927 from 19th-century oral tradition

title: Good King Wenceslas
origin: Words John Mason Neale (1853) to the 13th-century spring carol 'Tempus adest floridum' (Piae Cantiones, 1582); first verse only
publicDomainBasis: Published 1582/1853; Neale d.1866

title: Molly Malone (Cockles and Mussels)
origin: Song attributed to James Yorkston, published in Cambridge, Massachusetts (1884); first verse only, without the chorus
publicDomainBasis: Published 1884; traditional attribution, no author living in 1931 known

title: Auld Lang Syne
origin: Words by Robert Burns (1788, published 1796); traditional Scottish tune, printed with the words by George Thomson (1799)
publicDomainBasis: Published 1796-99; Burns died 1796

title: Daisy Bell (Bicycle Built for Two)
origin: Harry Dacre (1892); chorus only
publicDomainBasis: Published 1892; Dacre died 1922

title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik
origin: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Serenade No. 13 in G, K. 525 (1787, published 1827), first movement opening theme; instrumental
publicDomainBasis: Composed 1787, published 1827; Mozart died 1791
